Cater

/KAY-ter/ � rhymes with 'later' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To cater to someone is to shape what you offer or do around their particular needs or preferences.

The menu caters to every diner, with vegan, spicy, and kids' options.

Worked Example

The hotel concierge catered to each guest's preferences by remembering their favorite room temperature, preferred pillow types, and breakfast orders from their previous stays.

Cater is precise here because the concierge isn't just providing service�she's actively shaping what she offers around each guest's specific needs and preferences. The whole service is adjusted to fit individual tastes. That's exactly what cater means.

How Cater Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

provide

provide: to supply something that is needed

accommodate

accommodate: to adjust to fit someone's needs

indulge

indulge: to give in to someone's wishes

Antonyms

standardize

standardize: to make everything identical for everyone

neglect

neglect: to ignore someone's needs completely

How Strong Is It? — provide → serve → accommodate → cater

provide vs. cater

provide vs. cater: Provide is the most basic level of this scale: to provide is simply to supply something, while to cater is to shape everything you offer around one person's particular wants.

serve vs. cater

serve vs. cater: Serve is stronger than provide but still weaker than cater: serving means attending to someone's general needs, while catering means tailoring what you offer to their specific preferences.

accommodate vs. cater

accommodate vs. cater: Accommodate comes close to cater but stops short: to accommodate is to adjust so someone's needs are met, while to cater is to go further and build what you offer entirely around them.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cater

Root — cater: buyer of food and provisions (Middle English catour, from Old French acater, 'to buy') (Old French / Middle English)

Put it together

Put it together: Cater began as the Middle English catour — the household servant whose whole job was buying food and provisions for others. Supplying exactly what people need grew into today's meaning: shaping what you offer around someone's particular needs and preferences.

Use the root in a new word: caterer

Use the root in a new word: caterer: The caterer planned and supplied every dish for the wedding — a caterer's whole job is to cater, shaping the food around the hosts' wishes.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Cater means to actively shape what you offer or do around someone's particular needs or preferences. Use it when you're adjusting your entire approach or menu, not just saying yes to a request. 'Serve' means providing; 'cater' means adjusting.
